churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, formatting, and layout are each behind one well-defined module with no reliance on framework internals, which is the hard part done right. The deductions are the 810-line server.mjs mixing routing with view composition and raw API-shape access, plus five copy-pasted error-handling blocks that a Hono v5 onError migration would have to touch five times.

findings.issue: The same 'catch (error) { if (error instanceof NotFoundError) return c.html(String(notFoundPage()), 404); throw error; }' block is duplicated in five route handlers (lines 567, 599, 647, 705, 796).
findings.suggestion: Centralize it: either app.onError mapping NotFoundError to the 404 page once, or a small withNotFound(handler) wrapper. This also pre-aligns with Hono v5's middleware-style onError signature.

findings.issue: fetchJson calls fetch() with no AbortController or timeout; a stalled API server hangs the page request indefinitely, and the pending promise stays in the cache.
findings.suggestion: Wrap upstream fetch in AbortSignal.timeout(ms) (or an AbortController with a timer) so a slow API degrades instead of hanging; the existing cached() promise-invalidation already handles the throw path.

findings.issue: View code reaches directly into deep raw PokeAPI JSON shapes (sprites.other['official-artwork'] at 343, varieties at 111-112, version_group_details at 120/142), so an API shape change or field rename ripples across many spots in server.mjs instead of one module.
findings.suggestion: Normalize responses into small domain objects (species, pokemon, moveRow) inside lib/api.mjs, the existing data-access boundary, so consumers depend on app-owned shapes.

findings.issue: All three dependencies are pinned to exact versions with no ranges, so patch/security releases (e.g. the serveStatic path-decoding fix shipped in hono 4.13.11 / node-server 2.1.3) require a manual bump.
findings.suggestion: Use caret ranges (^4.13.14, ^2.1.5, ^2.0.11) and rely on package-lock.json for determinism in CI.

findings.issue: htmx 2.0.11 is npm's 'latest' tag, but htmx 4.0.0 (fetch-based internals, released 2026-08-28) is the new major line; the attributes used here (hx-get/hx-target/hx-swap/hx-sync/hx-trigger) are unchanged, so migration risk is low.
findings.suggestion: Fine to stay on 2.x today since the htmx team has not moved npm 'latest' to 4.0; track 4.x and switch when it becomes the default, which should be a drop-in for this attribute set.

findings.issue: Static assets (htmx.min.js, styles.css, tokens.css) are served with no Cache-Control headers; browsers revalidate on every navigation.
findings.suggestion: Pass onFound to serveStatic to set Cache-Control (or let the reverse proxy own it explicitly) — cheap to add now, annoying to retrofit.

findings.issue: app.onError((error, c) => ...) uses the v4 signature, which Hono v5 (currently 5.0.0-rc.1, per hono.dev/docs/guides/migrating-to-v5) changes to a (c, next) middleware with the error on c.error.
findings.suggestion: No action needed while on stable v4; just note that the eventual v5 upgrade touches app.onError and app.notFound signatures — the rest of the codebase (Hono, html, serve, serveStatic) survives v5 unchanged.

summary: This app ages well: it pins the exact current stable releases of Hono (4.13.14) and its Node adapter v2 (2.1.5), uses current import paths (serveStatic from @hono/node-server/serve-static, hono/html), keeps htmx at the npm-latest 2.0.11 line, and carries only three necessary dependencies with htmx self-hosted from node_modules. Data access, formatting, and layout are each confined to one module with no reliance on framework internals, so framework upgrades would touch very few files. The main forward-looking gaps are the absence of an upstream fetch timeout, five duplicated NotFound→404 blocks, deep raw-JSON access in the 810-line server.mjs, and exact version pins that postpone security patches.
